name: Yerba Buena Cove: Montgomery St to Sansome St
ring: Montgomery St & Broadway; Sansome St & Broadway; Sansome St & Market St; 2nd St & Market St; 2nd St & Folsom St; New Montgomery St & Howard St; Montgomery St & Market St
note: 1847 beach ran along Montgomery St (Clark's Point at Broadway/Battery to Rincon Point). Includes Laguna Salada (Montgomery & Jackson), filled 1849 (Dow p.30 citing Bancroft). Storeship Niantic beached at Clay & Sansome in 1849; the old waterfront was buried by fill after the 4 May 1851 fire (NPS). Band dates: medium confidence.

name: Yerba Buena Cove: Sansome St to Battery St / 2nd to 1st St
ring: Sansome St & Broadway; Battery St & Broadway; Battery St & Market St; 1st St & Market St; 1st St & Folsom St; 2nd St & Folsom St; 2nd St & Market St; Sansome St & Market St
note: Storeships General Harrison (Clay & Battery) and Apollo burned in the May 1851 fire and were buried in fill (NPS). City grades adopted 1853 because the shore had advanced ~1000 ft east of the 1850 grade (Dow pp.31-32). Interpolated band; refine with USCS 1853/1857 T-sheets.

name: Yerba Buena Cove: Battery St to Front St / 1st to Fremont St
ring: Battery St & Broadway; Front St & Broadway; Front St & Market St; Fremont St & Folsom St; 1st St & Folsom St; 1st St & Market St; Battery St & Market St
note: By 1852 filling 'carried out with planned precision'; steam paddy and sand cars ran down Battery St dumping sand between California and Clay (LeCount & Strong 1854 directory, quoted by Dow pp.30-31). Steam paddy filling of tidelands 1852-1873 (NRHP Embarcadero nomination). Interpolated band.

name: Yerba Buena Cove: Front St to Davis St / Fremont to Beale St
ring: Front St & Broadway; Davis St & Broadway; Davis St & Market St; Beale St & Folsom St; Fremont St & Folsom St; Front St & Market St
note: Filling of the cove and sale of water lots continued until 1859 (Exploratorium); 'within fifteen years of [1850] most of Yerba Buena Cove had been filled' (Dow p.56). Interpolated band.

name: Yerba Buena Cove: Davis St to old East St waterfront (first seawall)
ring: Davis St & Broadway; The Embarcadero & Broadway; The Embarcadero & Washington St; Steuart St & Market St; Steuart St & Folsom St; Beale St & Folsom St; Davis St & Market St
note: Outermost cove lots up to the 1851 waterfront line (East St, now west half of The Embarcadero). First (old) seawall built along this line Sept 1867-1869: Pacific-Washington, Washington-Market, Market-Mission (Dow pp.35-36). Medium-low confidence on start year.

name: New seawall + Embarcadero roadway, Broadway to Mission St
ring: The Embarcadero & Broadway; @37.79950,-122.39728; @37.79693,-122.39500; @37.79494,-122.39409; @37.79408,-122.39217; Steuart St & Mission St; Steuart St & Market St; The Embarcadero & Washington St
note: Second seawall (200 ft outside the 1851 line, authorised 15 Mar 1878): sections 5 (1884-85), 6 (1885-86), 7 (1887-89), 8b (1888-90, to foot of Mission), 8a (1891-92) (Dow Appendix 6). Only ~4 acres of new land here because the new wall lay just outside the old one (Dow p.39). Ferry Building (1896-98) sits on this line.

name: Seawall + fill, Mission St to Harrison St (Rincon Point)
ring: Steuart St & Mission St; @37.79408,-122.39217; @37.79279,-122.39084; @37.79123,-122.38992; @37.78970,-122.38800; Spear St & Harrison St; Spear St & Folsom St; Steuart St & Folsom St
note: Seawall sections 8 (Dec 1909-Mar 1910), 9a (Jan 1913-Nov 1914), 9b (Jan 1913-May 1915, Folsom-Harrison) (Dow App. 6). Fill behind wall largely 1906 rubble and dredged mud (Dow p.54). Rincon Point itself (Harrison & Spear) was natural land.

name: East of Rincon Hill: Main/Beale to The Embarcadero, Harrison to Brannan
ring: Spear St & Harrison St; The Embarcadero & Harrison St; The Embarcadero & Brannan St; Delancey St & Brannan St; Beale St & Bryant St; Beale St & Harrison St
note: Mid-1850s wharf/fill on the half block Bryant-Harrison-Spear (Ham & Hathaway; Bache 1856-57 map); Pacific Mail moved to a new wharf at First St in the late 1860s (Dow pp.49-51). Low confidence: dates bracket scattered fills shown on USCS charts.

name: Seawall + fill, Harrison St to King St (South Beach)
ring: The Embarcadero & Harrison St; @37.78970,-122.38800; @37.78722,-122.38731; @37.78495,-122.38756; @37.78203,-122.38789; The Embarcadero & King St; The Embarcadero & Brannan St
note: Seawall sections 9 (Feb-Oct 1910), 10 (1909-11), 11 (1909), 11a (1908-14), 12 (Jun 1907-Jun 1908, Brannan/Townsend-King) (Dow App. 6). State gained >10 acres; fill probably 1906 ruins + dredged mud (Dow pp.53-54).

name: South Beach / Steamboat Point: Brannan to King, 2nd to Embarcadero
ring: Delancey St & Brannan St; The Embarcadero & Brannan St; The Embarcadero & King St; 3rd St & King St; 3rd St & Townsend St; 2nd St & Townsend St
note: Citizens' Gas Co. filled block Townsend/King/2nd/3rd from 1864; Union Lumber Assn (SP) filled block 1st/2nd/Townsend/Brannan from 1867 using the 111-ft Steamboat Point hill; by 1871 more wharves + ferry slip; 'by the mid-1880s ... acres of filled land' (Dow pp.50-52).

name: King St to Berry St, east of 3rd St (seawall section 13)
note: Seawall section 13 (30 Dec 1903 - 27 Apr 1905), foot of King to south of Berry, first wall built under the 1903 $2M bond (Dow p.53). East edge approximate.

name: Berry St to Channel St, east of 3rd St (Pier 46B block; now Oracle Park east)
note: Seawall 13a (Feb 1922-Jan 1924) plus a caisson seawall along Channel St; Third Street Wharf removed and the block Channel/Berry/3rd filled with material dredged from Channel St (Dow pp.54-55).

name: Clark's Point / east base of Telegraph Hill to the seawall
note: Fill along the hill's east shore shown on USCS chart 621 of 1853; new seawall sections 1-4 built Sept 1878-Aug 1881 (Kearny to Front/Davis); fill behind wall 'limited and sporadic', completely reclaimed only about 1900; dredged mud pumped behind section 1 in 1879 (Dow pp.40-41, App. 6). Rock for the walls quarried from Telegraph Hill itself.

name: North Beach tidelands, Kearny St to Taylor St
note: Seawall section A (Dec 1879-Jan 1881) enclosed North Beach to Powell; section B (Sep 1890-May 1893) Powell-Taylor. Most tideland fill occurred 1906-1915 (USC&GS chart 5532, 1906 vs 1915), incl. 1906 earthquake debris (Dow pp.42-44). Year_start 1881 = first enclosure; consider weighting growth toward 1906-1915.

name: Fisherman's Wharf (Taylor St to Hyde St)
note: Fishermen's harbour at foot of Taylor built from May 1900 (section B extended 481 ft + Jones St breakwater); dumping inshore caused mud to flow into the harbour; bulkhead wharves on Jefferson and Tonquin 1914; breakwaters 1917 (Dow pp.43-44). Lagoon/boat basin stays water.

name: Pier 45 (built on a fill core)
note: Pier 45 begun 1928, completed early 1929: rock retaining wall filled with sand dredged alongside, 1,000 ft into the bay, then concrete deck on piles - 'built on filled land, a first for San Francisco's harbor' (Dow p.47). Ring approximate.

name: Aquatic Park: Hyde St to Van Ness Ave
ring: Hyde St & North Point St; Hyde St & Jefferson St; @37.80840,-122.42110; @37.80700,-122.42350; @37.80740,-122.42560; Van Ness Ave & North Point St
note: Belt Railroad embankment across Aquatic Cove Hyde-Larkin from Fort Mason tunnel rock (1912-14); 1906 brick from the Palace Hotel dumped on the beach; Van Ness Ave extension filled for the Municipal Pier (early 1930s); WPA seawall, beach and bathhouse completed 22 Jan 1939 (Dow pp.45-46). The cove itself stays water.

name: Fort Mason lower post (west side of Black Point, Gas House Cove)
note: Army quartermaster depot: seawall from the tip of Black Point westward then south, enclosing ~6-6.5 acres of Gas House Cove filled behind it; contract Nov 1908, work began early 1909 (Dow pp.48-49 citing Engineering Record 6 Aug 1910). Piers 1-3 beyond are pile-supported. Ring approximate.

name: Harbor View east: Fillmore St to Laguna St, Bay St to the bay
ring: Fillmore St & Bay St; Fillmore St & Marina Blvd; Webster St & Marina Blvd; Laguna St & Marina Blvd; Laguna St & Bay St
note: Piecemeal fill 1851-1906: Fillmore St wharf 1863, sand fill east of Webster by 1869, Phelps works 1882, SF Gas Light Co. pier (probably fill) 1891, seawall around J.G. Fair property by 1894, dump at Webster & Bay pre-1906. USGS fill-age classes 1851-69 / 1869-95 / 1895-1906 (USGS OFR 90-253 fig. 6).

name: Marina cove hydraulic fill (PPIE)
ring: Divisadero St & Chestnut St; Divisadero St & Marina Blvd; Fillmore St & Marina Blvd; Fillmore St & Bay St; Fillmore St & Chestnut St
note: Hydraulic fill of the remaining Marina cove 13 Apr - Sept 1912 for the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition (~70% sand / 30% mud pumped behind the old seawall); the rim of the cove had been filled 1895-1906 (USGS OFR 90-253). Liquefied in 1989.

name: Strawberry Island / slough, Lyon St to Divisadero St (PPIE grounds)
ring: Lyon St & Lombard St; Lyon St & Marina Blvd; Divisadero St & Marina Blvd; Divisadero St & Chestnut St
note: Exposition grading 1911-14: tidal slough and marsh filled; 6-8 acres under the Court of the Four Seasons filled by scrapers; Palace of Fine Arts lagoon kept as a remnant (USGS OFR 90-253 citing Todd 1921). Small roads/fills across waterways already by 1869.

name: Marina Green and yacht harbour, north of Marina Blvd
ring: Lyon St & Marina Blvd; @37.80800,-122.44830; @37.80900,-122.44400; @37.80880,-122.43900; @37.80720,-122.43400; Laguna St & Marina Blvd; Webster St & Marina Blvd; Fillmore St & Marina Blvd; Divisadero St & Marina Blvd
note: Exposition fill 1912 and further hydraulic/other fills through 1917 during site restoration (USGS OFR 90-253). Later: SERA/WPA basalt-block seawall 1930s; harbour entrance moved 1958; breakwater widened with ~45,000 yd3 of rubble Mar 1961-Mar 1963; Gas House Cove marina 1962 (Dow pp.75-77).

name: Crissy Field (Presidio bayfront marsh), Lyon St to Fort Point
note: Tidal marsh of the Presidio filled 1911-14 for the PPIE (Parks Conservancy); hydraulic fill west of Lyon placed by a sea-going dredge, <=6 ft deep (USGS OFR 90-253). Crissy Army Airfield 1921-1936 (NPS). Some sources say part of the marsh was filled in the 1870s - low confidence on start.

name: Crissy Field tidal marsh (restored)
note: 18-acre tidal marsh + 22 acres of dunes restored on the old airfield; work began 1999, marsh reopened to the tides 2000, project completed 2001 (NPS; ASLA). Ring = OSM/Overture 'Crissy Marsh' bbox.

name: Mission (SoMa) marshes: 3rd & Harrison to 8th & Howard
ring: 3rd St & Howard St; 3rd St & Townsend St; 7th St & Townsend St; Division St & 9th St; 9th St & Howard St
note: ~160-acre peat marsh NW of Mission Bay (3rd & Harrison to 8th & Howard) plus a parallel swamp near Mission & 7th-8th. Folsom St plank road filled across it 1852; Harrison St graded 3rd-8th by 1862 (150,000 yd3 of sand); steam paddy levelling 'between Sixth and Mission Dolores' in 1870 (Dow pp.82-86).

name: Mission Bay inside Long Bridge, Townsend St to Channel St
ring: 3rd St & Townsend St; 3rd St & Channel St; 7th St & Channel St; 7th St & Townsend St
note: Southern Pacific filled its Mission Bay lands from c.1869 (terminal moved to 3rd & Townsend; 'filling up the water channel formed by Long Bridge at the foot of Fourth Street', 1872 directory); by 1884 fill reached just beyond Channel St (Dow pp.88-89). Mission Creek channel (Channel St) stays water.

name: Mission Bay inside Long Bridge, Channel St to 16th St
ring: 3rd St & Channel St; 3rd St & 16th St; 7th St & 16th St; 7th St & Channel St
note: SP advanced the fill from Channel St toward 16th St in the 1890s; >2/3 reclaimed by 1902; completed with 1906 earthquake debris (Dow pp.89-93).

name: Mission Bay, 16th St to Mariposa St west of 3rd St
ring: 3rd St & 16th St; 3rd St & Mariposa St; Pennsylvania Ave & Mariposa St; 7th St & 16th St
note: After the 1906 debris removal SP had filled all its Mission Bay holdings including south of 16th to Mariposa west of Long Bridge (Dow p.93). End year approximate.

name: Mission Creek marshes behind Potrero Hill (to 20th & Harrison)
ring: 7th St & Townsend St; 7th St & 16th St; Potrero Ave & 17th St; Harrison St & 20th St; Harrison St & 18th St; Division St & 9th St
note: Salt marsh along Mission Creek inland to 20th & Harrison; died off and was filled around the turn of the century once Mission Bay fill cut off the tides (Dow pp.83, 90). Start year low confidence.

name: China Basin (Santa Fe), east of 3rd St, Channel St to 16th St
note: SF & San Joaquin Valley Ry (then Santa Fe) lease of ~35 acres; seawall trench dredged along the bulkhead line from May 1901, then 2.8 million yd3 of fill, mostly from Potrero Hill; 'remarkable engineering feat' in 1902 (Dow pp.90-92). End year approximate.

name: Point San Quentin / Central Basin, 16th St to Mariposa east of 3rd St
ring: 3rd St & 16th St; @37.76710,-122.38560; @37.76420,-122.38450; Illinois St & Mariposa St; 3rd St & Mariposa St
note: 8 acres east of Long Bridge filled by 1902, obliterating Point San Quentin; later ~4 acres at Central Basin (17th-Mariposa east of Illinois) reclaimed behind a rock wall (Dow pp.89, 93-94). Low confidence on end date.

name: Mission Rock / Pier 50 terminal
note: Two islets (0.15 acre) enlarged to ~4 acres by dumped rock 1878-1900 (California Dry Dock Co.); Pier 50 'Mission Rock Terminal' built 1947-31 Aug 1950 with concrete bulkhead around 6 acres and >500,000 tons of fill (Dow pp.94-96). Ring approximate; excludes Pier 48 north of the channel.

name: Potrero Point (Pier 70 area), Mariposa St to 23rd St east of Illinois
note: Pacific Rolling Mills granted 8 acres of tideland 1866 (mill done 1867); several blocks filled by Allardt's 1869 survey; tidelands auctioned 28 Feb 1871; SF Gas Light works 1872; California Sugar Refinery 1881 (3 tideland blocks filled); Union Iron Works moved here late 1884 (10 tideland blocks, about half filled) (Dow pp.99-103). Hill cut down for fill.

name: South of Potrero Point to Islais Creek (23rd St to Cesar Chavez St)
ring: Illinois St & 23rd St; @37.75500,-122.38200; @37.75050,-122.38000; Illinois St & Cesar Chavez St
note: Western Pacific filled its property south of the point, joining Potrero Point to the Islais Creek shore (Dow p.103, undated); WP's Islais Creek yard first unit c.1931 (Western Construction News, cited by Dow p.116). LOW confidence dates.

name: Islais Creek Reclamation District (280 acres)
ring: Iowa St & 25th St; 3rd St & 25th St; 3rd St & Cesar Chavez St; 3rd St & Marin St; Toland St & Evans Ave; Toland St & Oakdale Ave; Barneveld Ave & Oakdale Ave; Kansas St & Cesar Chavez St
note: District created by the Legislature 1925 (upheld Jan 1927): 2,090-ft rock seawall on the N side of Islais Creek from 3rd St to the SP trestle, 6.5 million yd3 dredged and placed, plus Bayshore Blvd and Western Pacific excavation spoil; 'took more than ten years' (Dow pp.112-116). Earlier: San Bruno toll road dike across the marsh (1850s-80s), Potrero & Bay View RR trestle 1866, Islais Creek wharf and 5 acres of fill on the S bank 1918-1920 (Dow pp.107-111). Channel stays water.

name: Army Street Terminal (Pier 80)
note: 68-acre terminal: 22 acres were an older city garbage-dump fill, 46 acres new; 4.3 million yd3; sand dike on rock in trenches 135 ft deep; begun Sept 1963, opened 1967 (Dow pp.117-119).

name: Boblitt debris dike / Piers 94-96 (India Basin north)
ring: 3rd St & Marin St; Illinois St & Marin St; @37.74780,-122.37650; @37.74500,-122.37100; @37.74080,-122.37100; Cargo Way & Jennings St; Amador St & Cargo Way
note: 5,800-ft debris dike (1.7M yd3 of construction rubble) begun 1962 around 22 blocks from Islais Creek channel south to India St (inshore edge Arthur Ave); 2.5M yd3 of Army St Terminal dredge mud behind it = ~150 acres; Pier 96 LASH terminal opened Feb 1972, Pier 94 begun 1972 (Dow pp.125-128). Pier 94 wetland later restored (see Heron's Head row note).

name: Pier 98 fill (Heron's Head)
note: Fill dumped in the 1970s for a planned Pier 98 terminal (never completed; described as illegal/unauthorised fill). Dates bracket 'the 1970s' - low confidence.

name: Heron's Head Park tidal marsh (restored)
note: Tidal marsh restoration permits 1998, construction complete by Dec 1999; ~7-8 acres of marsh (EcoAtlas project 5560). Only the low marsh/channels become marsh - the spit stays land. Ring = park bbox (OSM/Overture), approximate.

name: PG&E Station P (Hunters Point power plant) dikes
note: 85,000 yd3 of serpentine from the plant site used for two dikes out to the bulkhead line; first unit on line 3 Dec 1929; enlarged 1949 (Dow pp.124-125). Small; ring approximate.

name: India Basin, Innes Ave east of Evans (hurried 1965 fill)
note: ~25 acres filled hurriedly in 1965 near Innes Ave & Earl St to pre-empt BCDC restrictions (Dow p.125). Ring approximate.

name: Hunters Point Naval Shipyard fills (north & east)
note: Navy condemned 537 acres (by May 1942); Point Avisadero (170-ft hill) levelled and 5 million yd3 moved to the north and south parts of the yard; 1,092-ft dry dock 1942-43; small-craft docks 1943-44; yard grew to 979 acres (Dow pp.139-145). Earlier small fills at the tip: dry dock 1 (1866-68), dock 2 (1901-03), dock 1 enlarged (1916-18).

name: Hunters Point SW shore / South Basin north side
note: After WWII the submerged land south of Hunters Point was 'gradually filled with material from building and equipment foundations, sandblast waste ... Filling continues today' (Dow p.145, written 1973). Low confidence on dates.

name: Bay View Park race course (reclaimed marsh)
ring: 3rd St & Gilman Ave; Hawes St & Gilman Ave; Hawes St & Bancroft Ave; Bancroft Ave & 3rd St
note: Race course on reclaimed land protected by a seawall per 1864 directory; a veteran recalled dunes being cut down to fill low places c.1874 (Dow pp.151-152). Bounded by Third, Hawes, Bancroft, Gilman.

name: Double Rock Cove war housing fill (South Basin)
ring: Jennings St & Thomas Ave; Ingalls St & Thomas Ave; @37.72650,-122.38250; @37.72300,-122.38300; Ingalls St & Yosemite Ave; Jennings St & Yosemite Ave
note: 30 acres of tideland faced Double Rock Cove (Thomas, Jennings, Wallace, Yosemite, Bancroft, Ingalls); 200,000 yd3 from two local hills; 500 prefab dwellings; charts only show it in 1957 (Dow p.153). Ring approximate.

name: Small cove NE of Candlestick Point (Gilman & Griffith playground)
note: Tiny cove gone by the 1934 chart; city bought the site 1932 for a playground (Dow p.152). Ring approximate.

name: Candlestick Cove (SW side of Candlestick Point)
note: Marsh on the 1934 chart, dry land by 1958; SF Housing Authority built 944 temporary units on 102 acres here by 1944 (Dow p.154). Demolished by 1980 (SFPUC).

name: Candlestick Park stadium and parking fill
note: ~500,000 yd3 already dumped on Harney's tidelands when the stadium contract was signed 24 Jul 1958; another 1.5M yd3 for the 50-acre parking lot, much from cutting Bay View hill; stadium opened 1960 (Dow pp.155-156). Parking lot 'built entirely on rubble and fill' (SFPUC).

name: South Basin shoreline fills after 1965 (Yosemite Slough / Candlestick Point SRA)
note: City issued many fill permits just before BCDC jurisdiction began 17 Sept 1965; unauthorised fill continued at South Basin into the 1970s (Dow pp.150, 156). Low confidence.

name: Treasure Island (artificial, on Yerba Buena Shoals)
note: Army Corps of Engineers began 11 Feb 1936 and finished 24 Aug 1937 (other sources: 7 Feb 1936 - 4 Sep 1937); ~400 acres, ~20-29 million yd3 of dredged sand/mud inside ~287,000 tons of rock seawall (Treasure Island Museum; Living New Deal). Yerba Buena Island is natural.

name: Ocean Beach: O'Shaughnessy seawall, Esplanade and Great Highway
ring: Point Lobos Ave & 48th Ave; @37.77985,-122.51200; @37.77500,-122.51330; @37.76400,-122.51220; Great Highway & Lincoln Way; Great Highway & Balboa St
note: Not bay fill: a concrete seawall/esplanade built on the beach in sections 1915/16-1928/29 (first 1,500 ft done Nov 1916); Great Highway paved 1929 (Wikipedia; NPS). Only matters if the c.1800 ocean shoreline sits east of today's. Low.

name: Embarcadero piers band (pile-supported), Pier 45 to China Basin
note: TIGER counts piers as land. Everything here outside the seawall is pier deck on piles (exceptions: Pier 45 fill core, see sf_pier45). Piers were built as each seawall section was finished (1880s-1910s) and most were rebuilt or given their present bulkhead facades 1912-1938 (NRHP Embarcadero nomination). Pier 39 opened as a retail pier 4 Oct 1978 on an earlier cargo pier. Use per-pier dates from the NRHP nomination if needed.

name: SP Bayshore Cutoff causeway & Bayshore Yard (Visitacion Bay west)
note: Bayshore Cutoff built Oct 1904 - Dec 1907 with fill trestles across Visitacion Cove (Nov 1905 photo); Bayshore Yard substantially complete by 1921 (Wikipedia). Ring approximate.

name: Brisbane Lagoon landfill (SF municipal dump) + US-101 causeway
note: SF municipal landfill 1932-1967 filled the part of Brisbane Lagoon east of the tracks and west of US-101; ~600 acres, 40 ft deep (Wikipedia; FoundSF). US-101 moved onto a new fill causeway 1955-56 (Bayshore Cutoff article). Ring approximate.

name: Sierra Point landfill / office park
note: Tidelands at Sierra Point used as SF's next sanitary landfill after Brisbane: dumping from late 1966 (FoundSF) / operated 1965-1972 (SF Bay Water Board staff report); later an office park. Ring approximate.

name: Oyster Point landfill / marina (South San Francisco)
note: 57-acre Class III landfill operated 1956-1970 on the bay margin; Oyster Point Marina/Park built on it afterwards (SF Bay Regional Water Board order R2-2017-0046). Ring approximate.

name: SFO: Mills Field 1927 - reclaimed marsh pasture east of the Bayshore Highway
note: Tidal marsh on the 1892 survey (sloughs to the railroad); the 'cow pasture' of the Mills estate dairy leased by the city 15 Mar 1927 (150 acres; SFO Museum) and dedicated 7 May 1927 as Mills Field. Ring = the part of the c.1800 marsh (SFEI poster) east of the old highway that is land on the 1939-photo sheet: the airfield's part of it (inside the 1939 dike) is 152 acres, i.e. the 1927 lease; the rest is the pasture north of it. Reclamation date between the 1892 survey and 1927 unknown: ESTIMATED bracket midpoint 1905-15 (dry pasture well before the 1927 field). Topo: USGS 1:62,500 San Mateo 1899 (1892 survey) and 1943 (1939 photos); 1:24,000 San Francisco South / Montara Mountain / San Mateo (1946 photos), + Hunters Point 1956, 1968 PR, 1973 PR (TNM historical topo GeoTIFFs).

name: SFO / San Bruno / Millbrae: reclaimed marsh pasture between the railroad and the Bayshore Highway
note: c.1800 / 1892 tidal marsh between the upland and the old Bayshore Highway, South San Francisco to Millbrae; drained pasture with ditches on the 1939-photo sheet (Mills estate dairy land). Date ESTIMATED as for sm_sfo_mills_pasture_field (between the 1892 survey and the 1927 lease). Ring = c.1800 marsh (SFEI poster) within the area, simplified to 12 m. Topo: USGS 1:62,500 San Mateo 1899 (1892 survey) and 1943 (1939 photos); 1:24,000 San Francisco South / Montara Mountain / San Mateo (1946 photos), + Hunters Point 1956, 1968 PR, 1973 PR (TNM historical topo GeoTIFFs).

name: SFO: tidelands reclaimed in the early 1930s (diked airfield on the 1939 sheet)
note: City bought the Mills Field land and tidelands 1930-31 (renamed San Francisco Airport 9 Jun 1931); 'in the early 1930s, 350 acres of tidelands was reclaimed and by 1935 the airport had extended its runway C from 1,900 feet to 3,000 feet' (FoundSF / SFO Museum); PWA bond for the tideland reclamation (Living New Deal). Ring = the dike outline of the airfield on the 1939-photo 1:62,500 San Mateo sheet minus the c.1800 marsh (= 230 acres here). Spread over the bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: seaplane harbour shores, Coast Guard Air Station and north field
note: Marsh on the 1939-photo sheet; land on the 1946-photo sheets. WPA work Oct 1935 - Aug 1939: 'dredging for seaplane harbor; building seaplane wharves, ramp and seawalls, rock and earth levees' (Healy via Living New Deal); Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco commissioned 15 Nov 1940 (militarymuseum.org). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: seaplane harbour shores, Coast Guard Air Station and north field
note: Marsh on the 1939-photo sheet; land on the 1946-photo sheets. WPA work Oct 1935 - Aug 1939: 'dredging for seaplane harbor; building seaplane wharves, ramp and seawalls, rock and earth levees' (Healy via Living New Deal); Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco commissioned 15 Nov 1940 (militarymuseum.org). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: seaplane harbour shores, Coast Guard Air Station and north field
note: Marsh on the 1939-photo sheet; land on the 1946-photo sheets. WPA work Oct 1935 - Aug 1939: 'dredging for seaplane harbor; building seaplane wharves, ramp and seawalls, rock and earth levees' (Healy via Living New Deal); Coast Guard Air Station San Francisco commissioned 15 Nov 1940 (militarymuseum.org). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: 1939-43 landing-field extension and wartime hydraulic fill
note: Bay and marsh on the 1939-photo sheet, airfield on the 1946-photo sheets (1:24,000; the Hunters Point quad was not mapped in 1946: there the wartime field is taken as the airports/ SFO-1946 pavement zone). WPA 'Landing Field Extension Fill' 1939 (Living New Deal); Army lease 5 Feb 1942, 'additional land was created by hydraulic fill' for three hard runways, the longest 8,000 ft (USACE 1991 via militarymuseum.org). Pavement on it is dated 1944 (data/manual/airports). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: 1939-43 landing-field extension and wartime hydraulic fill
note: Bay and marsh on the 1939-photo sheet, airfield on the 1946-photo sheets (1:24,000; the Hunters Point quad was not mapped in 1946: there the wartime field is taken as the airports/ SFO-1946 pavement zone). WPA 'Landing Field Extension Fill' 1939 (Living New Deal); Army lease 5 Feb 1942, 'additional land was created by hydraulic fill' for three hard runways, the longest 8,000 ft (USACE 1991 via militarymuseum.org). Pavement on it is dated 1944 (data/manual/airports). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: 1939-43 landing-field extension and wartime hydraulic fill
note: Bay and marsh on the 1939-photo sheet, airfield on the 1946-photo sheets (1:24,000; the Hunters Point quad was not mapped in 1946: there the wartime field is taken as the airports/ SFO-1946 pavement zone). WPA 'Landing Field Extension Fill' 1939 (Living New Deal); Army lease 5 Feb 1942, 'additional land was created by hydraulic fill' for three hard runways, the longest 8,000 ft (USACE 1991 via militarymuseum.org). Pavement on it is dated 1944 (data/manual/airports). Bracket, estimated.

name: SFO: shoreline additions 1946-56 (south-east seawall)
note: Water on the 1946-photo sheets, land on the 1956 sheets (small pieces along the south-east shore; part may be sheet registration, +-20 m). Before the 1953 south-end pavement. Estimated.

name: SFO: shoreline additions 1946-56 (south-east seawall)
note: Water on the 1946-photo sheets, land on the 1956 sheets (small pieces along the south-east shore; part may be sheet registration, +-20 m). Before the 1953 south-end pavement. Estimated.

name: SFO: shoreline additions 1946-56 (south-east seawall)
note: Water on the 1946-photo sheets, land on the 1956 sheets (small pieces along the south-east shore; part may be sheet registration, +-20 m). Before the 1953 south-end pavement. Estimated.

name: SFO: fill for the 1961 extension of runway 28L
note: Bay ('mud') on the 1956 sheets, land and runway on the 1968 photorevision; 28L lengthened 1961 onto new fill (data/manual/airports). Estimated.

name: SFO: fill for the 1968 extension of runway 28R
note: Mud on the 1968 photos, land and paved on the 1973 photorevision; 28R extended 1968 (pavement 1969, data/manual/airports). Estimated.

name: SFO: fill for the 1968 extension of runway 28R
note: Mud on the 1968 photos, land and paved on the 1973 photorevision; 28R extended 1968 (pavement 1969, data/manual/airports). Estimated.

name: SFO: fill for the 1968 extension of runway 28R
note: Mud on the 1968 photos, land and paved on the 1973 photorevision; 28R extended 1968 (pavement 1969, data/manual/airports). Estimated.

name: SFO: north-east fill north of the wartime field
note: Not on a 1946 sheet (Hunters Point quad first mapped 1956), land and paved on the 1956 sheet; 28R 8,870 ft on the Aug 1952 chart. Before the 1951 pavement (data/manual/airports SFO-NE-fill). Estimated.

name: SFO: fill for the 1962 north extension of runway 1R
note: Bay on the 1956 Hunters Point sheet, runway extension and loop taxiway drawn on the 1968 photorevision; 1R north extension onto the NE fill 1962 (data/manual/airports). Estimated.

name: Brewer Island diked for dairy (later Foster City)
note: Brewer's Island tidal marsh dry and protected from the bay 'since 1897 or earlier'; Frank Brewer diked and drained it c.1900-01 for a dairy (Wikipedia Brewer Island; Foster City Life).

name: Foster City hydraulic sand fill
note: Diked Brewer Island raised with ~18 million yd3 of dredged sand in the 1960s (lagoon left as drainage); first residents 7 Mar 1964; incorporated 27 Apr 1971 (Foster City; Wikipedia). End year = incorporation, approximate.

name: Redwood Peninsula salt ponds (later Redwood Shores)
note: Leslie Salt bought two small Redwood City salt plants in 1907 and acquired the Redwood Peninsula in 1928 to add to its ponds (sources conflict). LOW confidence dates.

name: Redwood Shores fill over former salt ponds
note: Leslie Properties proposed the city 1963 and began filling its evaporation ponds; built up 'in the 1960s'; Bank of America owner 1972; sold to Mobil 1973 (Wikipedia; rwc-localhistory). Marine World 1960s-1986.

name: Bair Island salt-pond levees
note: Leslie Salt built levees 1948-1952 splitting Bair Island into Inner, Middle and Outer Bair (Bay Nature 2008).

name: Bair Island returned to tidal action
note: Outer Bair levees failed from the 1970s/1983 once maintenance stopped; planned Outer Bair breaches 2008; Inner Bair breached 10 Dec 2015 (SF Bay Wildlife Society; SM Daily Journal). Animate east->west if possible.

name: Oakland Long Wharf / Oakland Mole (Oakland Point)
note: Central Pacific pier extended and renamed Long Wharf 1868, opened 16 Jan 1871; rebuilt 1879-80 as a rock-and-earth mole (~1 million yd3 from Fruitvale and Niles Canyon), opened 1882 (Wikipedia). Ring approximate.

name: Key System mole / Bay Bridge toll plaza fill
note: Key System formed 1903 with a rock mole + pier into the bay; the Bay Bridge distribution structure/toll plaza built on the mole area in the 1930s (bridge opened Nov 1936). LOW confidence: mole partly trestle.

name: Oakland Outer Harbor & Oakland Army Base
note: Tidelands near the Key Route Basin filled from c.1910 (City of Oakland), continued after 1925 (Port of Oakland); the remainder filled only in WWII when the Army built Oakland Army Base (construction 1941, opened 8 Dec 1941) (BRAC/DENIX). Outer Harbor terminals and the Army base lie between the Mole and the Bay Bridge approach; ring approximate.

name: Naval Supply Depot Oakland (Middle Harbor)
note: Oakland voters agreed in 1936 to donate 390 acres; land sold/transferred to the Navy 1940; Middle Harbor dredged to 50 ft and fill placed to create the depot on former tidal flats; opened 15 Dec 1941 (Wikipedia; Port of Oakland). Ring approximate.

name: Middle Harbor Shoreline Park habitat (partial restoration)
note: Park opened 2004 (Wikipedia says 2003) on part of the closed depot; Middle Harbor enhancement placed dredged sediment to create shallow-water/eelgrass habitat (Port of Oakland). Ring approximate; mostly subtidal habitat, not marsh.

name: Tidal Canal (makes Alameda an island)
note: 1.5-mile canal cut through the neck of the Alameda peninsula from San Leandro Bay to the estuary; excavated 1889-92 and 1901-03, Alameda celebrated becoming an island 15 Sept 1902 (HMdb marker; Alameda Post). Ring is a coarse box - clip to TIGER water.

name: Naval Air Station Alameda (Alameda Point)
note: Curtiss-Wright site deeded to the Navy 1 Jun 1936; hydraulic fill of tidelands with sand dredged from the bay and estuary 'early 1930s through early 1940s'; station commissioned 1 Nov 1940 (Alameda Post; City of Alameda). ~2,500 acres at closure.

name: Alameda South Shore fill (Utah Construction)
note: Utah Construction bought the South Shore tidelands 1950; its dredge arrived Nov 1955 and filled beyond the old seawall (Alameda Post). End year approximate.

name: Bay Farm Island / Harbor Bay Isle fill
note: Utah Construction held Bay Farm by 1954; its dredge placed 22 million yd3 at Bay Farm for a reclamation district (1968 report); Harbor Bay Isle Associates formed 1972 to build on it; fill joined the island to the mainland (Alameda Post). The original asparagus-farm island (natural) is excluded by the data.

name: Oakland Airport North Field
note: Oakland bought 680 acres in Apr 1927; 7,020-ft runway built in 21 days; dedicated by Lindbergh 17 Sep 1927 (Wikipedia). Site was marsh/low land at Bay Farm Island - medium confidence that this is 'fill' vs marsh conversion.

name: Oakland Airport South Field (runway 12/30)
note: 1962 $20 million expansion on bay fill incl. the 10,000-ft runway 11/29 (now 12/30) (Wikipedia). Start year approximate.

name: Berkeley waterfront landfill / Marina / Cesar Chavez Park
note: City waterfront dump from 1923 (or late 1920s); diked municipal landfill from 1957, closed to waste 1983, sealed 1991 and opened as North Waterfront (Cesar Chavez) Park (KQED; Wikipedia). Marina built progressively on the fill.

name: Albany Bulb / Albany landfill
note: Construction-debris dump 1963-1987 (some sources: to 1983) (Wikipedia).

name: Richmond Kaiser shipyards and Inner Harbor fills
note: Kaiser Richmond Yards 1-2 basins and ways (outline: data/manual/industrial_sites kaiser_yards_1_2): Yard 1 begun Dec 1940, Yard 2 1941; Yard 1 begun Dec 1940; yards 2-4 1941-42; ~4 million yd3 of fill incl. 215,000 yd3 of rock to make ground over ~100 acres (HAER via Wikipedia). Richmond's deep-water port developed 1929; Santa Fe tracks on fill at Ferry Point c.1900 (NPS trail). Ring is coarse - also covers 1912-29 Inner Harbor work (low confidence).

name: Richmond Kaiser shipyards and Inner Harbor fills
note: Kaiser Yard 3 (permanent basin yard, Point Potrero; outline: industrial_sites kaiser_yard3), built 1941-42. Was one box with the whole Inner Harbor (1940.9-1943), which pushed the 1931 Ford plant and ~40 older buildings to 1941-43 (military/industrial audit); the rest of the Inner Harbor now takes the fb_east_bay bracket, dated by the buildings on it (Ford Point before the 1931 plant, the Santa Fe yard before 1900).

name: Marinship (Sausalito) on Richardson Bay mudflats
note: Bechtel contract 12 Mar 1942; a hill was cut down and dumped on the Richardson Bay mudflats; first keel laid 27 Jun 1942; 300-ft x 1.5-mile channel dredged (Sausalito Historical Society; Wikipedia).

name: Corte Madera / Larkspur / Greenbrae marsh fills
note: Marsh islands levelled late 1940s for Redwood High School fill; Greenbrae Marina subdivision and Marina Village built on fill c.1950s; Army Corps dredge spoils dumped along Bon Air Rd late 1960s (Friends of Corte Madera Creek). LOW confidence.

name: Hamilton Field baylands diked (farmland, then airfield)
note: Former tidal salt marsh 'drained and farming began over 100 years ago' and diked from tidal flooding (Federal Register 1998); Army airfield operations from Dec 1932, completed 1935. Start year LOW confidence.

name: Hamilton wetland restoration
note: Levee breached 25 Apr 2014 returning ~648 acres of the former airfield to tidal action 'for the first time in over a century' (Coastal Conservancy / Army Corps). Only the runway/marsh basin, not the developed base.

name: Sonoma baylands (Petaluma River to Sonoma Creek) diked for hay & grazing
note: Diking for hay/oats/dairy began in the Gold Rush/early American period; Sears Point lands 'diked in the mid-1800s', flooded again in 2015 'for the first time in about 140 years' (CDFW; Sonoma Land Trust). Range LOW confidence.

name: Sears Point tidal restoration
note: Sonoma Land Trust breached the levee 25 Oct 2015 (285-ft opening), flooding a ~1,000-acre basin of the 2,237-acre ranch. Ring approximate.

name: Lower Napa River marshes diked for hay & dairy
note: Tide and baylands reclaimed for hay and dairy from the early American period (CDFW Napa-Sonoma Marshes Wildlife Area). Range LOW confidence.

name: Leslie Salt ponds, lower Napa River
note: In the 1950s Leslie Salt expanded into the North Bay creating ~10,000 acres of salt ponds near the mouth of the Napa River (CDFW). Mostly on already-diked hay land - use to switch cover to salt_pond.

name: Napa River Salt Marsh / Napa Plant Site restoration
note: State bought the Napa salt ponds from Cargill (2003-2004 era); Napa Plant Site north unit breached to Fagan Slough 13 Oct 2008 (>200 acres); further breaches through ~2015 (CDFW; Coastal Conservancy). Range medium-low.

name: Suisun Marsh levees (farming, then duck clubs)
note: Grizzly Island etc. leveed and farmed (asparagus, sugar beets, grain, hogs); converted to managed duck-club wetlands in the 1900s; 'by about 1930, waterfowl hunting had become the primary use' (Wikipedia Suisun Marsh); Reclamation District 1607 formed 1914. Start year LOW.

name: East Bay salt ponds (Alvarado / Mt Eden / Union City)
note: First South Bay solar salt ponds built by John Johnson 1853 (Eden Landing area); 18 salt companies by 1868, merged into Leslie Salt by the Depression; about half the South Bay's tidal marsh converted to ponds by the 1930s (Wikipedia SF Bay Salt Ponds). Range medium-low.

name: Newark / Alviso / Sunnyvale / Mountain View / Ravenswood salt ponds
note: Diking of South Bay marshes for salt 'began in the 1920s and 1930s and was completed by the mid to late 1950s' (City of San Jose / H.T. Harvey baylands report).

name: Alviso Island Ponds A19-A21 breach
note: 15,100 acres bought from Cargill 2003; the Island Ponds (A19-A21, between Coyote Creek and Mud Slough) were the first South Bay Salt Pond Restoration Project breach (2006). Ring approximate - clip to ponds.

name: Eden Landing ponds E8A/E9/E8X breach
note: 630 acres reopened to the bay Sept 2011; by then the project had restored nearly 3,000 acres of ponds to tidal action (South Bay Salt Pond Restoration Project). Ring approximate.

name: San Francisco fallback
note: FALLBACK - use only for fill/diking not covered by a specific zone. Bay Area fill was concentrated 1850-1965; the Army Corps found 243 sq mi of 'reclaimable' baylands already reclaimed by the late 1950s, and filling largely stopped after the McAteer-Petris Act created BCDC in 1965 (KQED). LOW confidence; consider distance-from-1850-shore as a proxy for age.
